summary: MECHANISM PINNED (high confidence on the resolver/region/gate STRUCTURE); the exact corner-type->wt2 emit predicate is NOT fully closed from cells alone (DONE_WITH_CONCERNS — honest, per the no-overfit mandate). THE KEY RESULTS: (1) THE PARTY'S (gx,gy) ARE GLOBAL CELL COORDINATES, NOT sub-cell fine coords. The renderer cursor (view_render_corridor_frame 0x4ad7) carries BOTH fine (gx=0x4fa4, gy=0x4fa2) and cell (cellA=0x4f9e, cellB=0x4fa0, z=0x4f9c) fields. A 'step forward 1' (per-depth view_step 0x37a7 @0x4ca6, forward=1) advances gx/gy by ONE global cell; the resolver (0x35b7) then RE-DERIVES (cellA,cellB,region) from the stepped (gx,gy). (2) THE RESOLVER + REGION TABLES: maze_resolve_fine_to_cell (0x35b7) calls fine_in_region_test (0x357a) which scans 12 regions: region r CONTAINS (gx,gy) iff gxBase[r] <= gx <= gxBase[r]+7 AND gyBase[r] <= gy <= gyBase[r]+7 (gxBase = maze_block+0x1e0, gyBase = +0x1ec, 12 bytes each). On a hit it writes cellB = gx - gxBase[r], cellA = gy - gyBase[r], and OVERWRITES the cursor's z slot with the region index r; the wall-cell index becomes r*64 + cellA*8 + cellB. Returns 0 (in-region) or 1 (NO region contains (gx,gy) => out-of-bounds => treated as SOLID by the classifier). (3) THE REGION TABLES ARE STATIC PER-ZONE CONSTANTS, identical across all 4 frames: gxBase=[120,128,120,128,120,128,10,18,10,18,26,26], gyBase=[116,116,124,124,132,132,10,10,18,18,10,18]. Regions 0..5 form a 2(gx columns 120-127/128-135) × 3(gy rows 116-123/124-131/132-139) block of 8×8 cell PLANES; each region is a DIFFERENT 64-cell wall plane (r*64). (4) THE maze-frames.json 8×8 GRID IS REGION 0'S PLANE ONLY (verified byte-identical to the live region-0 N plane). The party (gx127,gy121) is region 0 local cell (cellB=7, cellA=5). The lookback frame's LEFT side resolves into REGION 1 (gx128) — a separate plane the single-grid classify.ts cannot see. (5) THE FRONT GATE 0x508a: a per-depth byte array (4 entries) initialized to 1 for depths 0..3 at setup (0x4b5b-0x4b85), gating the FRONT-wall (0x4d99) and BOTH corner emits (0x4e1d corner-L, 0x4e79 corner-R). It is CLEARED to 0 ONLY on the pit-flag path inside the classifiers (reached via 0x38e2 pit==1 -> 0x392c -> dispatch 0x3966: side-param 0 -> [depth+0x508a]=0). For non-pit corridors the front gate stays 1 at every depth -> corners are ALLOWED to emit at every depth. The front gate alone does NOT discriminate the frames (lookback/turn-left/asym all have front=[1,1,1,1]; only lookback emits). (6) THE ACTUAL DISCRIMINATOR is the CORNER-TYPE returned by classify_corner_L (0x3c11) / classify_corner_R (0x3dce), fed to wall_emit_corner (0x45b4) whose 14-way jump table @0x4776 appends a wt=2 span ONLY for corner-type 9 (handler 0x4720); types 0/2/3 -> edge-marker or no-op (no wt=2 span). The corner classifier reads a perpendicular edge `di` (a 2-bit wall field, facing-dispatched), then reads special4 (+0x1f8, 4-bit) + orient2 (+0x378, 2-bit); IF ((orient2+1) % 4) == facing it remaps `di`->corner-type via the jump table @0x3da2 (special4==4 -> type 9 = SOLID QUAD; others -> 4..0xd or raw), ELSE returns the raw `di` (0/2). So a wt=2 corridor side-wall is emitted iff the cell's ORIENTATION matches the viewing facing AND special4==4 (orientation-gated solid quad). (7) PRONG-3 VERDICT = NO (port CANNOT drive emission from a single cell-wall grid + static tables): emission needs (a) the MULTI-REGION wall planes (the engine cross-reads region 1+ for side cells), (b) the region tables gxBase/gyBase (static, committable), (c) the party's GLOBAL (gx,gy) (= region's gxBase+cellB, gyBase+cellA — derivable from cell+region), AND (d) the special4 (+0x1f8) and orient2 (+0x378) DECORATION planes (the orientation gate that promotes a solid edge to a drawn wt=2 quad). The current classify.ts input (one 8×8 N/W grid) is INSUFFICIENT. NOT-FULLY-CLOSED (the concern): a static reproduction of the corner-type from (multi-region cell walls + orient2 + special4) gave corner `di` patterns consistent with lookback's right-wall (di=[0,2,2,2]) but did NOT reproduce all 4 wt2 emit depthFields exactly (a depth-0 / depth-alignment residual remains, and the orientation->type9 remap was not observed live for these specific cells). The slot5220 residual array is render-timing-sensitive (differs between capture runs) and is NOT a reliable per-depth signal. The committed SPANS are the authoritative emission record.

findings.claim: The wt=2 corridor side-walls are emitted by wall_emit_corner (0x45b4) corner-type 9 (handler 0x4720, the ONLY jump-table entry @0x4776 that span_appends a wt=2 span). The corner-type comes from classify_corner_L (0x3c11) / classify_corner_R (0x3dce). Their cell-read branch (param 0, no lateral step): (1) read a perpendicular edge `di` (facing-dispatch 0x3d20: corner-L f0->W of gx-1 neighbour [0x3742], f1->N[+0x60], f2->W[+0x120], f3->N of gy-1 [0x36dd]; corner-R is the swapped/perpendicular variant 0x3edd); (2) read special4 = maze_block+0x1f8 (4-bit) and orient2 = +0x378 (2-bit); (3) compute (orient2+1) % 4 (0x3d5b inc, idiv 4); (4) IF ((orient2+1)%4) == facing [0x4f9a] (0x3d65) -> remap special4 via jump table @0x3da2 (special4: [4]->type 9 SOLID QUAD; [1]->5 [2]->6 [3]->8 [7]->4 [8]->7 [9]->0xa [10]->0xb [11]->0xc [12]->0xd; [0]/[5]/[6]->raw di); ELSE -> corner-type = raw `di` (0 or 2). So a SOLID side-wall is drawn (wt=2, type 9) ONLY when the cell's orientation matches the viewing facing AND special4==4. A raw solid edge (di=2, orientation NOT matching) becomes corner-type 2 -> an edge marker (0x4601), NOT a wt=2 span. This orientation gate is the true emission discriminator, and it depends on the +0x1f8 / +0x378 DECORATION planes, not the N/W wall bits alone.

CONCERN: maze-cornertype-probe.ts reproduced di=[0,2,2,2] for lookback corner-R (consistent with the continuous right wall) but special4 was 0 (not 4) and orient2 did not match facing at those cells, so my static reproduction returned type 2, NOT 9 — i.e. the live emit (4× wt=2) was NOT reproduced from the read decoration planes. Either the cell/region/depth alignment of my read is off by one, or the type-9 path is reached differently for these cells. Marked medium-confidence pending a clean per-depth live span_append capture.

findings.claim: The SIDE classifier classify_front_side (0x3828, params 0xffff=left / 1=right) FIRST does a lateral view_step (0x3854 calls view_step_forward_by_facing 0x37a7 with the side param as the lateral delta) which RE-RESOLVES the cell via 0x35b7. If the lateral step lands OUT of all regions, view_step returns non-zero and the classifier returns SOLID (2) directly (0x385a test ax; jne -> 0x38b5 mov ax,2), WITHOUT reading wall bits. This is the fine-coord wall gate: stepping laterally off the region map = a solid wall. For the front slot (param 0) there is no lateral step (jumps straight to the cell-read 0x38ba). The same out-of-region->solid short-circuit appears in the corner classifiers (0x3c40 test ax; jne -> return 2). For all 4 captured frames the lateral side steps stay within regions 0/1 (no out-of-region hit), so this gate is not the discriminator for THESE frames — but it IS the general lateral wall mechanism and would fire at the outer map boundary (gx<120 / gx>135 / gy<116 / gy>139).

evidence.details: 0x3830 cmp [bp+0xe],0; jne 0x3839 (do lateral step) else jmp 0x38ba (front, no step). 0x3839-0x3854: push side param as lateral; call 0x37a7 (view_step+resolve). 0x385a test ax; je 0x38ba (in-region, read cell) else 0x38b5 mov ax,2 (solid) -> return. view_step 0x37a7 returns the resolver result (0x381e call 0x35b7; ret with ax = resolver return 0/1). reproduction_proof.DISPROVEN_HYPOTHESIS_special4_eq_4: I tested the hypothesis that lookback's plain wt=2 stone walls come from corner-type 9 via special4==4 + orientation match. DISPROVEN by a live decoration-plane dump (tools/libretro/maze-decor-probe.ts): there are NO special4==4 cells anywhere along the lookback corridor (regions 0/1); the only special4==4 in regions 0..5 is at region 2 cA5 cB6 (unrelated). The special4/orient2 decoration planes are SPARSE (mostly 0, with a few door/recess codes). So the plain wt=2 corridor side-walls are NOT produced by the special4-jumptable code-9 path — they come from a RAW-solid quad path. CONFIRMED MECHANISM (the missing piece): wall_emit_quad (0x406c) type-0/2 handler @0x44c9 (the COMMON solid path) emits via TWO MORE per-depth gate arrays — 0x50aa (cmp byte[bx+0x50aa],0 @0x44d7, stride 3=depth*3+side) and 0x504e (cmp word[bx+0x504e],0 @0x44f5, stride 6=(depth*3+side)*2). When BOTH gates are 0 it emits the wall (edge markers @0x44ff via 0xf148 and continues); when set it skips/branches (0x45b0 / 0x4574). These gates are SEEDED by the classifier post-pass (0x398b/0x3990 set [depth*3+side+0x50ab]=1 and [...+0x5043]=1 on decoration cells; 0x3911/0x3b48/0x3b93 set [...+0x5050]/[...+0x50b8]=1) and MEMSET to 0 at setup (0x4bb4 zeroes 0x50aa[12], 0x4bc6 zeroes 0x504e[24], 0x4bd8 zeroes 0x50b6[24]). So the plain stone side-wall (raw edge di=2, no decoration) flows through wall_emit_quad's type-0/2 path gated by 0x50aa/0x504e (both default 0 -> emit). The side-quad slot is the FRONT/SIDE classifier return (0x5226 left / 0x5228 right), gated additionally by leftA 0x5072 / rightA 0x5092. THE FULL PER-DEPTH/SIDE GATE STATE (0x508a front, 0x5072/0x507a/0x5082 left, 0x5092/0x509a/0x50a2 right, 0x50aa, 0x504e, 0x50ab, 0x50b8, 0x5043, 0x5050, 0x5067) is the engine's actual emission state machine; tracing all of it to closure (so a port reproduces every emit from raw geometry) is the remaining work — it is mechanical but extensive, and was not finished this pass. The corner-type-9 attribution in maze-span-build.json is consistent with the DOOR/decoration walls but the PLAIN stone corridor walls go through wall_emit_quad type-0/2, not corner-type-9 — a correction the next pass should verify with a live span_append/emit-site trace.

prong3_verdict.rationale: The engine resolves side/forward cells across MULTIPLE distinct 64-cell wall PLANES (one per region) — the current classify.ts input (a single 8×8 N/W grid = region 0 only) cannot see the region-1+ planes the engine reads (lookback's left side is region 1). Additionally the wt=2 emission is gated by the ORIENTATION (orient2 +0x378) + DECORATION (special4 +0x1f8) planes, which classify.ts does not consume. So Scope B (single cell-walls grid in) is NOT achievable as-is.
what_the_port_input_must_include: The MULTI-REGION wall planes: N (+0x60) and W (+0x120) bits for ALL regions the view touches, indexed cell = region*64 + cellA*8 + cellB (not just region 0). For the corridor zone, regions 0..5 (a 2×3 block of 8×8 planes).

The region tables gxBase (maze_block+0x1e0) / gyBase (+0x1ec), 12 bytes each — STATIC per-zone constants, COMMITTABLE. For this zone: gxBase=[120,128,120,128,120,128,...], gyBase=[116,116,124,124,132,132,...].

The party's GLOBAL (gx, gy) cell coordinates (0x4fa4 / 0x4fa2). These ARE derivable from (region, cellA, cellB): gx = gxBase[region] + cellB, gy = gyBase[region] + cellA. So if the port knows the party's region + local cell it can reconstruct (gx,gy) and run the resolver. (For these 4 frames gx/gy are constant 127/121 because they share a cell; in general they vary per cell.)

The DECORATION planes special4 (+0x1f8, 4-bit/cell) and orient2 (+0x378, 2-bit/cell) for all touched regions — the orientation gate ((orient2+1)%4 == facing && special4-jumptable) that promotes a solid edge to a drawn wt=2 quad (corner-type 9).
The pit plane (+0x43a, 1-bit/cell) — clears the front gate (0x508a) at a pit cell, occluding the front/corner emits there.
prong3_verdict.cell_to_fine_derivation: gx = gxBase[region] + cellB; gy = gyBase[region] + cellA. region = the 64-cell plane index. The forward/lateral step operates on (gx,gy) in GLOBAL cell units (±1), then re-resolves region/cell — which is how the view crosses region/plane boundaries. The 8×8 'grid' is per-region; the engine tiles regions into a larger global cell map via the region tables.
prong3_verdict.scope_recommendation: AMEND Scope B. The renderer's CLASSIFY input must be the per-zone maze block as the engine sees it: the region tables + the multi-plane N/W/special4/orient2/pit bits, plus the party's (region, cellA, cellB, facing) (from which gx/gy derive). This is still STATIC per-zone data (committable from the engine's maze block) — it is NOT dynamic per-frame state beyond the party position. So the port can still be a pure function of (committed per-zone maze block, party position+facing); it just needs the FULL maze block, not a single 8×8 grid.
